paper.tagline: Inspections, cases and notices from the Beeblecraft Inspection Office

columns.caption: The south line near the cherry trees: birch slab lanes, the rail down the middle, a copper lantern on every pillar.

columns.headline: The office starts work
columns.body:
The Beeblecraft Inspection Office is choosing where to settle and will build its office as soon as it can. In the meantime it works out of the community house at spawn.
The office mainly inspects public builds and places: rail lines, roads, farms, services and outposts. It also takes requests for private inspections of bases and operations. File one with the office directly, or reach the officer any way that works for you. Each visit is written up as a report, and each problem gets a case number so it can be followed until it is fixed. This gazette is where the reports are published.

columns.caption: Heading back toward spawn across the water, with lanterns along the right side.

columns.headline: South line: a clean ride and one sore head
columns.body:
Ridden out to z 10121 and back on 2 October. The cart never stalled, and there were no stray carts. It kept going through every stretch satellite imagery could not see.
Birch slabs on the outer lanes, stone brick in the middle. Copper lanterns hang from lightning rods on stone brick pillars six to nine blocks apart, and the tunnels add froglights. On one stretch through the desert the outer lanes change to dark wood.
One fault: a block at head height at a base exit on the way out. Case C-006.

columns.caption: The south line through the desert, set out with spruce trees and lanterns on the sand. The outer lanes here are dark wood.

columns.title: From the officer's desk
columns.body:
I began by riding every line out of spawn, both ways, with a notebook on my knee. All four are done.
The south road is the best public road out of spawn in this world, and whoever hung those lanterns has my thanks. The west line goes under the sea and out to x -9995 without a single stall. The east hill at x 6207 is the one place a cart will not get you home, so that is the first job.
If you left an empty cart on a line, please take it with you. It stops the next rider dead.
Reports and cases are open to anyone who asks.

columns.caption: The four lines out of spawn, to scale, measured to the end of the rails or the road.
A south line bridge with a lattice railing and lit powered rails. A second bridge of sandstone and wood runs alongside.

columns.text: Continued on page 2: the west line ridden to the end, the east and north lines and the case register.

columns.caption: The west line on a raised stretch of dark wood lanes, with lanterns hung from wooden arches high over the forest and the sea.

columns.headline: West line: under the sea to x -9995
columns.body:
Ridden out to x -9995 and back on 2 October. The cart did not stop once in either direction, and there were no stray carts.
From x -1468 the line runs into a long tunnel under the ocean. The tunnel is why satellite imagery lost the track at x -3870 and saw less than half the line. The ride covered the rest.
The outer lanes are stone brick with smooth stone in the middle. Bridges switch to wood, mostly jungle planks with dark oak down the middle. Further out the track passes a maze.
No cases from this ride.

columns.caption: Inside the tunnel under the ocean, with kelp outside the glass and a lit powered rail ahead.

columns.headline: On the west line
columns.caption: A plank bridge over a river, with a village on the far bank.
The track climbs stairs toward a mossy stone brick temple.

columns.title: Still to check
columns.body:
A second railway leaves the west line near the tunnel entrance at x -1468. Where it goes is not known yet.
The west road runs on about 10 blocks past the rails. The end will be measured on the next visit.

columns.headline: East line: stall at x 6207
columns.body: Rails run to x 8747 and the road on to x 9210. Heading east there were no rail problems. Heading home the cart stops on the hill at x 6207 and rolls back. It is a 16 block climb with no powered rails, while climbs of 12 and 14 further out rode fine. The hill with tunnels from x 1806 to 3283 hides the track from satellite imagery, and the ride through it was clean. Stray carts as well. Cases C-001, C-003, C-004.

columns.headline: North line: slow hill, fine tunnel
columns.body: Rails to z -7385, road to z -7433. One slow climb at z -2769 heading out, otherwise clean both ways. A climb of 15 at z -2142 rode fine. The tunnel from z -4197 runs under the sea, with a window to the water, paintings on the walls and flowers along the track. Cases C-002, C-003.

columns.caption: The maze beside the west line, seen from the cart.

columns.title: Case register
columns.lines:
C-001 East stall, x 6207
C-002 North hill, z -2769
C-003 Stray carts on lines
C-004 East rails to road end
C-005 Powered rail standard
C-006 South head bump
